What is in the basket

Each strategy runs on Tradetron at the lots set here. Change a strategy's lots and every figure on the page is recomputed from its Tradetron trades. Set a strategy to 0 to take it out.

Headline figures at every cost level

Gross is the price P&L before any cost. Tradetron net deducts statutory charges and Tradetron's 0.05% slippage. Then ₹20 brokerage per order. All-in also deducts slippage of max(0.1 pt, 0.5% of the fill) per fill. Percentages are of the capital shown at the top of the page.

Tail risk

VaR is the loss exceeded on only 5% (or 1%) of days. CVaR is the average loss on those worst 5% of days.

And which strategies moved the basket that day. A dot means the strategy closed nothing that day.

The 10 best days

P&L by weekday

Booked on exit day. NIFTY's weekly expiry fell on Thursday until Aug 2025 and on Tuesday from Sep 2025 (a day earlier in holiday weeks), so expiry-day strategies bunch on those days and the positional straddle exits the day before.

Diversification

Why the strategies work better together

Strategies that make and lose money on different days shrink the basket's drawdown below the sum of their own.

Correlation

Near 0: independent. Positional strategies book P&L on exit day, so daily figures understate overlap; weekly is the fairest.

Intraday vs positional

Each sleeve's share of the margin, of the profit and of the risk (its covariance with the basket's daily P&L over the basket's variance).

Correlation on the basket's worst 5% of days

Short-premium strategies tend to lose together exactly when the market breaks, and a correlation over all days hides that. This takes the basket's worst 5% of days and measures the correlation inside them. Picking days by the basket's total pulls the correlation inside them below zero even for strategies with nothing in common, so every figure sits next to what independent strategies give: the same strategies, each with its days shuffled, 200 times.

Margin

How much capital the basket actually ties up

Each trading day's peak margin in use, rebuilt minute by minute from the Tradetron trades. These are estimates, not a broker's SPAN: spreads at max(0, width − credit) × qty + 2% of the short strike's notional; naked shorts at the strategy's margin figure spread over its short lots when fully deployed; +2% on shorts on their own expiry day from 20 Nov 2024.

Peak margin in use, every day

NIFTY expiry days stand out because the expiry-day strategies all trade then.

Expiry days against other days.

Average margin in use, month by month

Each strategy's margin figure times the share of that month's days it held a position.

Out-of-sample

Before the strategies were chosen

The 5-year runs (Sep 2021 to Sep 2026) are where the strategies were chosen and tuned. The holdout runs cover the 1.7 years before, which were never used to choose anything.

Risk rules

Portfolio stops and the rulebook

All-in, always: these levels decide when to stop trading, so they use the figures that include every cost.

Pausing new trades after a bad month or a deep drawdown

A day stop on the intraday sleeve

Tradetron's Portfolio Management can exit a group of deployments when their combined P&L for the day hits a loss. Tradetron's trades hold each leg's entry and exit, not its path in between, so the data can't replay a day that dipped below a level and recovered. It shows how the intraday sleeve's days closed.

Risk rulebook

Each level sits just beyond the worst this basket's backtest has seen, so none of them would have cost anything in 2020–26. They exist for the day the backtest hasn't seen. Tighter levels were tested above and cost more than they saved.

Per-strategy review and pause levels

Drawdown from the strategy's own live peak, at its lots. Hedged spreads are never set below one position's median defined max loss, so they don't fire on one ordinary losing trade.
